reviews.one_line_contribution: That per-item credit for retrieved experience is reference-dependent, and that the reference matching the actual decision a memory system makes is not the hole left by leave-one-out but the retriever's next-ranked item backfilling the slot — measured in a multi-step agent (ALFWorld, Qwen3-32B) at ±5 net, with the hole-vs-backfill gap, the gap against a static-exemplar reference, and the additivity error of each reference against realized two-item pruning reported in net points.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two verified threats, at different levels. (i) Setting: CUE-R, arxiv:2604.05467 (verified via s2cli, 2026-04-07, cit 2) already does intervention-based per-evidence utility with REMOVE/REPLACE/DUPLICATE — it is single-shot RAG with distractor replacement, so the specific 'replace with the retriever's own next candidate, in a sequential agent, tied to a pruning decision' move is not made there; that limits but does not remove the threat, since a reviewer will read this as CUE-R's REPLACE arm with a better-chosen replacement. (ii) Concept: the claim that a removal 'hole' is the wrong reference because it is not a plausible state is old and settled in the attribution home literature. arxiv:2110.11929 (verified, 'Double Trouble', AACL 2021, cit 7) shows deletion-metric bias and compares LOO against MLM-synthesized plausible counterfactuals; arxiv:2508.14482 (verified, 2025-08-20) formalizes exactly this as 'semantic missingness' — a baseline must represent a plausible state, not merely absent signal; arxiv:2607.14271 (verified, 2026-07-15) names the reference as one of five specification choices. The proposal cites the latter two but frames them as gaps rather than as the source of its central insight. What survives as new is narrow but real: the reference is chosen not for plausibility but for decision-equivalence (it equals what pruning re-retrieves), and it is evaluated against a downstream sequential outcome rather than a faithfulness metric. That is an incremental specification of a known point, not a new one. I also note arxiv:2605.21768 (Memory-R2, 'Fair Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon Memory-Augmented LLM Agents', 2026-05-20, found via s2cli) which the Related Work does not cite; it is RL training credit rather than counterfactual item value, so it is an omission in coverage rather than a collision.
reviews.strongest_objection: The three 'references for the same slot' are not matched on position or set size, so the headline ordering s(H1) < s(S1) < s(B1) confounds reference type with prompt geometry. F = [1,2,3] (new content at position 1, 3 items); H1 = [2,3] (2 items); B1 = [2,3,4] (new content at position 3, 3 items); S1 = [x,2,3] (new content at position 1, 3 items). B1 is a faithful simulation of pruning — that part is right — but the proposal's own prose ('the retriever's next candidate placed in the emptied rank-1 slot') is false: nothing occupies slot 1 in B1, item 2 promotes into it and item 4 appends last. So g_1 = s(B1) − s(H1) is 'what does a third exemplar appended at the end add to a two-item prompt', which mixes the content of item 4 with a set-size/format effect, while sigma_1 = s(S1) − s(H1) gives the static content the primacy slot. Given that position effects in retrieval-augmented prompting are large (the brief's own scan cites arxiv:2605.27105 on position/context-size effects), a reviewer can explain the entire predicted ordering without any claim about references. Second, related: the confirm/falsify bands leave the modal outcome undecided. The proposal's own nested-k prior says items 4–7 add only +2 to +4 net on top of [1,2,3]; P1 predicts item 4 alone adds ≥ +8 on top of a two-item set, and its falsifier requires g_1 ≤ 0 with the CI excluding +8. A measured g_1 of +4 — arguably the most likely value — confirms nothing and falsifies nothing, and the same (0, band) dead zone recurs in P3 (0–12), P4 (0–8) and P5, where the automated entailment check already flagged the falsifier as near-entailed. Third, the title claims 'only backfill predicts what pruning realizes', but the confirmatory arms only realize per-game, one- or two-item pruning from a frozen k=7 log; bank-level pruning, which couples games through shared items and is the decision real systems make, is arm R1, explicitly non-confirmatory and run only if time remains. The headline is therefore not tested at the granularity it claims.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Add a position-matched backfill arm B1_pos = [4,2,3] (item 4 promoted into slot 1) alongside B1 = [2,3,4], and/or a position-matched static arm S1_end = [2,3,x]; report g_1 and sigma_1 with the position factor crossed, so the reference claim is separated from prompt geometry. This is one extra 1,644-episode arm (~82 min) and the budget already has headroom. (2) Re-band the predictions so the likely outcome decides them: state P1 as a two-sided partition (confirm g_1 ≥ +6, falsify g_1 ≤ +2 by TOST against ±3 versus zero) rather than confirm ≥ +8 / falsify ≤ 0, and do the same for P3, P4 and P5 (the entailment check's fix for P5 — falsifier at g_1' ≤ 0 or TOST on g_1 − g_1' against ±3 — should be applied to all four). (3) Promote R1 (prune every validation rank-1 item from the bank, re-retrieve) from leftover-time fidelity check to a confirmatory arm with a pre-registered equivalence margin on s(B1) − s(R1), or retitle the paper to claim per-game pruning only. (4) Credit the removal-based-explanation literature explicitly (arxiv:2110.11929, arxiv:2508.14482) and state the delta as decision-equivalence of the reference, not as the discovery that references matter.
reviews.missing_baseline: A content-controlled third-item reference: a random or bank-matched irrelevant item (or a duplicate of item 2, i.e. CUE-R's DUPLICATE) placed in the same position as the backfill item, token-matched. Without it, g_1 cannot distinguish 'the retriever's next candidate specifically carries +8 net' from 'any third exemplar restores the three-shot format the reader expects', which is the cheapest alternative explanation of P1 and hence of the headline P3. The proposal has token-matched placebos everywhere else (static within 15%, wrong-procedure within 5%) but leaves precisely the arm carrying its mechanism unplacebo'd. A secondary omission: no leave-one-out at any slot other than rank 1 and rank 2 outside the pairwise arm, so the 'slot property' assertion in the hypothesis is never checked at a second slot.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision. The proposal's own check is above average for this round — four queries, channel named for each, IDs given, negative results reported as negative rather than as evidence — and it is right that nothing in the agent-memory or RAG literature makes this claim. But it is incomplete on the axis where the idea actually comes from: its 'home' query used feature-attribution vocabulary yet returned only baseline-taxonomy papers, missing the empirical NLP work that already shows LOO disagreeing with plausible-replacement references. My queries (all channel (a) s2cli, S2+HF both ok; WebSearch unavailable this session): 'counterfactual reference for removing a retrieved item: hole versus replacement by next-ranked candidate' --recent → 8 hits, nothing on the claim (arxiv:2604.05467, arxiv:2608.22856, arxiv:2506.20854); 'leave-one-out estimate overstates the effect of deleting a document because the retriever backfills the slot' → 12 hits, all unlearning / KV-eviction / LOO-distinguishability (arxiv:2309.17310, arxiv:2502.15082), nothing on retrieval backfill; 'CUE-R intervention-based per-evidence utility remove replace duplicate retrieval-augmented generation' → arxiv:2604.05467, arxiv:2605.01302 (CoRM-RAG), arxiv:2608.23252 (causal context allocation) — none uses the next-ranked candidate as reference; 'choice of baseline reference value in removal-based feature attribution changes the ranking of inputs' → arxiv:2110.11929, arxiv:1910.04256, arxiv:2402.09164; 'input marginalization plausible replacement versus zero baseline deletion metric text explanation' → arxiv:2110.11929 (AACL, cit 7), arxiv:2412.17512 (BEE, learned baselines); 'pruning a memory bank item is backfilled by the next retrieved item so per-item utility mis-estimates the pruning effect' --recent → empty (2 irrelevant hits); 'data valuation removal of a training point versus replacement reference in retrieval corpora downstream decision' --recent → empty (5 irrelevant hits); 'per-item credit assignment for experience memory in LLM agents validated by ablating memory items ALFWorld' --recent → 12 agent-memory papers (arxiv:2605.21768 Memory-R2, arxiv:2607.21106 AttriMem, arxiv:2605.04811 TreeMem, arxiv:2603.04549 A-MAC, arxiv:2601.08435 Fine-Mem), none validating a per-item score against a counterfactual. ID verification: VERIFIED arxiv:2604.05467 (2026-04-07, cit 2), arxiv:2507.04480 (2025-07-06, PKDD/ECML Workshops, cit 7), arxiv:2607.14271 (2026-07-15, cit 1), arxiv:2508.14482 (2025-08-20), arxiv:2606.29502 (2026-06-28, cit 9), arxiv:2512.10696 (2025-12-11), arxiv:2607.22562 (2026-05-29, cit 1), arxiv:2605.04811 and arxiv:2605.01302 (both returned by search). COULD NOT VERIFY: arxiv:2509.12765 (DIG confidence gain) — not found on S2 or HF; it is load-bearing in the Related Work as one of the three hole-based estimators, and it is also the id the brief carries, so both should be re-checked. arxiv:2606.16285, arxiv:2605.30712 and arxiv:2603.05093 were not checked. Net: the collision check is a genuine search, not a formality, but it establishes novelty only against the agent/RAG axis; against the attribution-baseline axis the point is prior art, and the proposal should be scored on the decision-equivalence delta alone.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A net-point measurement on ALFWorld that per-item credit for a retrieved memory item is reference-dependent, and that the reference matching what pruning actually does is not the empty slot but the retriever's next-ranked candidate promoted into it, with a test of whether summed single-item credits predict the cost of pruning two items.
reviews.closest_prior_work: CUE-R, arxiv:2604.05467 (VERIFIED, s2cli/S2+HF: 2026-04-07, 2 citations). It is already an intervention-based per-evidence-item utility framework whose whole design varies the reference (REMOVE / REPLACE / DUPLICATE) and reports that the intervention type changes the item's measured utility; it also already supplies the evidence-role taxonomy for interpreting those differences. What it does not do is make the replacement the retriever's own next-ranked candidate, tie a reference to a downstream pruning decision, or run in a multi-step agent -- so it does not scoop the specific backfill reference, but it does scoop the framing claim 'per-item utility depends on which counterfactual you use', which is the conceptual half of this proposal. The mechanism half is older and also verified: arxiv:2011.03623 (Feature Removal Is a Unifying Principle for Model Explanation Methods, VERIFIED via s2cli/HF) organizes removal-based explanation exactly around 'how the feature is removed' as the first axis; arxiv:2508.14482 (VERIFIED, 2025-08-20) already argues in so many words that a baseline 'must not merely lack signal, but must represent a plausible state', which is this proposal's entire argument for backfill; arxiv:2607.14271 (VERIFIED, 2026-07-15, Local Additive Feature Attribution: A Mathematical Taxonomy and Reporting Checklist) already names 'reference' as one of five specification choices. The proposal cites the last two itself, which is honest but self-defeating: after those, the remaining contribution is the choice of one particular reference in one particular domain plus a number. I also checked arxiv:2507.04480 (VERIFIED, PKDD/ECML Workshops 2025-07-06, 7 citations, hole-based SHAP over RAG documents) and arxiv:2509.12765 (VERIFIED, InfoGain-RAG, EMNLP, 12 citations, document information gain), which the proposal characterizes correctly. arxiv:2605.01302 (CoRM-RAG) also VERIFIED via search. I could NOT verify 2606.29502 (UCOB), 2605.30712 (ExpSuite), 2606.16285 (HiMPO), 2512.10696 (ReMe), 2607.22562 (SF-AMS), or 2603.05093; 2605.04811 (TreeMem) did return in a search and is verified.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline claim is true by construction and the confirmatory content collapses onto one already-measured quantity. Backfill is DEFINED as what the frozen deterministic retrieval log returns after the item is pruned, so 'only backfill predicts what pruning realizes' cannot fail at the per-game level; the only arm that could break the identity (R1, actually prune the bank and re-retrieve, which couples games through shared items) is explicitly optional, non-confirmatory, and runs only if time remains. Strip the tautology and P3 reduces to P1, and P1 reduces to 'the rank-4 expert item is worth something when added to a 2-item set' -- whose sign the program's own nested-k sweep already reports for free (items 4-7 add +2 to +4 net on top of [1,2,3]; k1->k3, i.e. TWO added items, is only +6.8/+9.3 net). That same prior argues the true g_1 is roughly +3 to +5, and the design's own numbers then make the experiment undecidable: CI +/-5, confirmation at g_1 >= +8, falsification at g_1 <= 0 with the CI excluding +8. The a-priori most likely outcome lands in the (0, +8) dead band and decides nothing, and the same dead-band structure repeats for P3 (0 to +12 at +/-7) and P4. A reviewer will also note that P2's band (-10) is not tied to the program's measured effect -- the wrong-type placebo blind1 was only -3 net against k0 -- which violates the round's own binding rule that margins be stated against measured effects, and that the proposal itself concedes P2 and the class factor 'can say nothing about class x reference interactions', so the second-largest arm block buys nothing for the central claim.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Promote R1 to confirmatory and state a prediction on s(B1) - s(R1): that is the only measurement in the plan that tests, rather than assumes, that the frozen-log backfill equals what bank-level pruning realizes, and it is also where the interesting failure lives (shared items couple games, so per-game backfill can be right while the pruning policy is wrong). Also verify and report that the retriever has no MMR/diversity/dedup step, since rank-order refill equals re-retrieval only for a set-independent scorer. (2) Re-derive the bands from the measured k-curve instead of asserting +8/+12: with a prior of g_1 ~ +3 to +5 the design needs either a pre-registered three-way decision rule that covers the whole line (superiority above a threshold, TOST equivalence inside a margin, indeterminate outside both) or more seeds on fewer games so the rank-1 CI is +/-2 to 3. (3) Replace the class arm (P2), which the proposal admits is definitionally uninformative here, with the decision-level test the title promises: rank items by hole credit and by backfill credit, prune the bottom-m of the bank under each ranking, re-retrieve, and measure realized success. 'The two references disagree about which items to prune, and the hole ranking loses X net points' is a claim worth a paper; 'the two references differ by 8 net points at one slot' is a calibration note. (4) Add the content-free filler control below.
reviews.missing_baseline: A token-matched, content-free filler in the emptied rank-1 slot: a wrong-type or step-shuffled exemplar (the program already has blind1) placed where the backfill item goes, so that F, H1, B1 and the filler arm are compared at matched set size and matched prompt length. As written, g_1 = s(B1) - s(H1) contrasts a 3-item, longer prompt against a 2-item, shorter one, so it confounds the next-ranked item's CONTENT with the mere presence of a third demonstration and a few hundred extra tokens -- and the round's own binding rules demand token- and rate-matched placebos. Note that the S1 arm is token-matched but H1 is not, so the reported ordering s(H1) < s(S1) < s(B1) is partly a length ordering. Secondary omissions a reviewer would also name: a Shapley-under-hole vs Shapley-under-backfill contrast on a subsample (the brief lists Shapley as a ground-truth estimator, and 'which reference' applies to it too, so excluding it purely on cost is weak), and a random-rank backfill (fill the slot from rank 5-7 instead of rank 4) to show the gap tracks retriever rank rather than any additional expert item.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision found. My queries, all through the s2cli channel (Semantic Scholar + HuggingFace, both reported ok on every call; WebSearch unavailable in this session, WebFetch not used): (a) 'counterfactual reference baseline for removing a retrieved item: empty slot versus next-ranked replacement' --recent -> 7 hits, nothing on the mechanism (closest was CUE-R arxiv:2604.05467, plus arxiv:2609.01865, 2608.12652, 2506.20854); (b) 'per-item credit assignment for retrieved experience memory in LLM agents leave-one-out' --recent -> 11 hits, all system papers that score memory items without validating the score against any counterfactual (AttriMem 2607.21106, MemQ 2605.08374, TreeMem 2605.04811, A-MAC 2603.04549, Memory-R2 2605.21768, MemSifter 2603.03379, LUCID 2608.00017) -- consistent with the brief's stated gap; (c) 'choice of baseline value in feature attribution changes the explanation removal versus replacement' -> returned the XAI baseline literature including arxiv:2110.11929 (deletion-based metrics are biased relative to plausible MLM-synthesized replacements) and arxiv:2412.17512 (BEE, learned baselines), i.e. the reference-choice point is long established outside RAG; (d) 'explaining by removing unified framework how features are removed baseline distribution Shapley' -> arxiv:2011.03623, the canonical statement that removal-based explanations are parameterized by how the feature is removed; (e) 'marginal value of a document equals its value over the next best alternative in a ranked retrieval list' -> EMPTY for this mechanism (12 hits, all reranking architecture papers: GroupRank 2511.11653, E^2Rank 2510.22733, JointRank 2506.22262, Rank-K 2505.14432, 2411.11767); (f) 'deleting a document from a retrieval corpus promotes the next ranked document effect on downstream accuracy' --recent -> EMPTY for the claim (5 hits on retriever position bias and distractor dose: 2605.26578, 2605.10828, 2503.05037); (g) 'CUE-R intervention based per-evidence utility remove replace duplicate retrieved evidence' -> CUE-R 2604.05467 and CoRM-RAG 2605.01302, neither using the retriever's next candidate as the reference. On the proposal's own Preprint Collision Check: it is above the median for this pipeline -- four queries, channel named, IDs attached, recency restriction used on two, and an explicit statement that WebSearch was not used -- and its characterizations of CUE-R, 2507.04480 and 2607.14271 match what I verified. Two real weaknesses. First, it verified none of the roughly fourteen arXiv IDs it leans on; I verified 2604.05467, 2507.04480, 2607.14271, 2508.14482, 2509.12765, 2605.01302 and 2605.04811, and could NOT verify 2606.29502, 2605.30712, 2606.16285, 2512.10696, 2607.22562 or 2603.05093, so a non-trivial part of its 'nobody does this' argument rests on unchecked citations. Second, the home-vocabulary query it ran ('feature attribution baseline reference value choice') missed the canonical statement of its own mechanism (arxiv:2011.03623) and never searched the framing in which 'value over the next-best alternative' is a century-old idea (opportunity cost, VCG externality, cascade displacement in ranked lists) -- and my query (e) in that vocabulary came back empty for retrieval, which is the honest result but is a search the proposal should have run itself and reported. Empty searches here are reported as empty, not as evidence of novelty.

reviews.one_line_contribution: For a retrieved memory item in a fixed-k agent prompt, the per-item credit you get depends on what fills the emptied slot, and the proposal measures three references on the same ALFWorld (game, seed) units - hole (leave-one-out), backfill (the retriever's next-ranked item, which is what deleting the item from the bank actually realizes under a frozen deterministic retriever) and static exemplar - claiming hole credit over-states the value that pruning realizes by at least 8 net per item and by at least 12 net when two items are pruned.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Verified: arxiv:2607.14271 (Local Additive Feature Attribution: A Mathematical Taxonomy and Reporting Checklist, S2, 2026-07-15) already names the reference - what replaces the removed input - as one of five specification choices that determine an attribution, and arxiv:2508.14482 (semantic missingness for path-attribution baselines, S2, 2025-08-20) already argues the reference must be a plausible in-distribution state rather than a hole. The proposal cites both and its conceptual thesis is theirs; the increment is instantiating 'plausible state' as the retriever's next-ranked bank item and tying the reference to a pruning decision in a multi-step agent, which neither paper does. Operationally closest is CUE-R (arxiv:2604.05467, verified on both S2 and HF, cit 2), which does intervention-based per-evidence utility with REMOVE/REPLACE/DUPLICATE - but replaces with distractors, in single-shot RAG, with no refill semantics. Also relevant and uncited: 'True to the Model or True to the Data?' (arxiv:2006.16234, found via my query 2), which is the canonical statement that interventional vs conditional reference distributions give different Shapley values for the same feature, and arxiv:2110.11929, which shows deletion-based attribution metrics are biased relative to leave-one-out because the deleted input is off-distribution. Taken together these blunt the claim that 'which counterfactual is item credit' is a new question: it is a known question, and the proposal contributes a measurement of its magnitude in one environment rather than the question itself.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline (P3) is close to an arithmetic consequence of the mechanism (P1), so the design never independently tests 'which reference predicts realized pruning'. D_H = c_H(1) + [s(B12) - s(H2)], and if each emptied slot recovers g >= +8 from its backfill and additivity roughly holds, D_H ~ g_1 + g_2 lands near +16 by construction. The one genuinely open quantity - whether backfill credits themselves add up, D_B - is explicitly demoted to a non-confirmatory estimand. Compounding this: the direction of P1 is near-certain (adding item 4 to a depleted [2,3] can hardly hurt when the bank is procedure-redundant), so the only open question is magnitude, and the proposal's own nested-k prior says items 4-7 add just +2 to +4 on top of the full set. The most likely outcome is therefore 0 < g_1 < +8, which the pre-registration declares neither confirming nor falsifying; the same wide indeterminate zone sits under P4 (0 to +8) and P5 (-2 to +8, already flagged near-entailed by the automated check). A well-powered design whose modal result decides nothing is not a test. Second objection a reviewer will raise: the entire study is at rank 1, gated at c_H(1) >= +10, yet pruners delete low-value tail items, not the top-ranked one - so the reference gap is measured precisely where no pruning decision is ever made, and the operational framing ('only backfill predicts what pruning realizes') is validated on items nobody prunes.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Re-designate the headline: make backfill additivity (D_B, the TOST against +/-10) and the bank-level realization arm R1 (s(B1) - s(R1)) confirmatory rather than time-permitting leftovers - those are the two claims not already implied by P1, and R1 is the only thing that turns 'backfill is what pruning realizes' from an argument into a measurement. (2) Move the primary slot off rank 1: run the hole/backfill/static contrast at a mid or tail slot (rank 3, or a stratum of items whose hole credit is near zero) where pruning decisions actually occur, and report the reference gap as a function of the item's own credit level. (3) Close the indeterminate zones: state P1/P4/P5 as pre-registered interval claims (e.g. TOST that g_1 is inside or outside [+2,+4], the nested-k prior) instead of a one-sided band at +8 with a falsifier at 0. (4) Add the filler placebo below. (5) Broaden the collision check into the ranking/recommendation and corpus-pruning vocabularies, where 'delete an item and the next candidate is promoted' is routine.
reviews.missing_baseline: A token-matched filler arm at the emptied slot: [2,3,X] where X is an irrelevant, wrong-type or shuffled exemplar matched to item 4's token count - the program's own measured `blind1` wrong-type placebo generalizes directly, and Appendix B already makes token- and rate-matched placebos binding. As written, B1 = [2,3,4] carries three exemplars and more tokens than H1 = [2,3], so g_1 confounds 'the retriever's next candidate has content value' with 'any third exemplar, or simply more context, refills the slot'. If the filler recovers as much as the backfill, P1 survives numerically while its stated mechanism (bank redundancy, retriever quality) collapses, and P5's reader-invariance claim becomes uninterpretable. A second cheap arm - backfill drawn from a random bank item of the same type rather than the retriever's rank-4 - would separate retriever quality from slot occupancy at one re-run per unit.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision. Ten queries, all answered by the s2cli channel (S2 + HF, both reporting ok); WebSearch was unavailable in this session, so no section text was read. (1) 'counterfactual reference choice removing a retrieved document versus replacing it with the next ranked candidate' --recent: 4 results, nearest CUE-R arxiv:2604.05467; nothing on refill/backfill references. (2) 'baseline value choice in feature attribution affects downstream decision removal versus realistic replacement': 12 results, relevant older work arxiv:2006.16234, arxiv:2110.11929, arxiv:2311.00500 - reference choice as a known specification problem, none in retrieval or agent memory. (3) 'CUE-R intervention-based per-evidence utility remove replace duplicate RAG': CUE-R arxiv:2604.05467, CoRM-RAG arxiv:2605.01302, and arxiv:2608.23252 (The Laws of Context Allocation, 2026-08-24, causal measurement probe for evidence utilization plus submodular context scheduling) - the last is the nearest recent item the proposal's own check missed and should be addressed, though it does not compare references or model pruning realization. (4) 'pruning a document from the corpus re-retrieval replaces it with next ranked document data valuation' --recent: 5 results, all reranking efficiency, nothing relevant. (5) 'Shapley value attribution of retrieved documents sources in RAG': 10 results, none makes the claim. (6) 'confidence gain per document attribution DIG RAG': 8 results, none makes the claim. (7) 'remove and retrain benchmark deletion metric out of distribution retraining ROAR': returned only unlearning papers. (8) 'removing an item from a ranked slate promotes the next candidate counterfactual evaluation of item removal in recommendation': nearest is arxiv:2007.12986 (counterfactual slate evaluation with sequential reward interactions) - adjacent off-policy estimation, not per-item reference choice. (9) 'validating memory pruning decisions in LLM agents against counterfactual re-run leave-one-out ALFWorld' --recent: 11 results, none validates a pruning score against counterfactual re-runs. (10) 'does leave-one-out overestimate the cost of deleting a training example replacement effect' --recent: 4 results, unlearning only. ID verification: I verified arxiv:2604.05467 (S2+HF, 2026-04-07, cit 2), arxiv:2607.14271 (S2, 2026-07-15), arxiv:2508.14482 (S2, 2025-08-20), arxiv:2512.10696 ReMe (S2, cit 55), arxiv:2607.22562 SF-AMS (S2), arxiv:2606.29502 UCOB (S2, cit 9), arxiv:2605.04811 TreeMem (S2), arxiv:2605.01302 and arxiv:2605.27105 (HF). I could NOT verify arxiv:2507.04480 (Shapley source attribution in RAG) or arxiv:2509.12765 (DIG confidence gain) - both returned 'not found on S2 or HF' by direct id lookup and did not surface under two targeted topical queries. That is a real weakness rather than a formality: those two are named in the Related Work as the hole-based foils that the whole contribution is defined against, so two of the four pillars of the novelty argument are currently uncheckable. Judging the proposal's own Preprint Collision Check: it is above the norm for this pipeline - four queries, channels named, IDs given, negative results reported as negative rather than as proof of novelty - but it is narrow in exactly the direction that matters. Its 'home' query covered feature-attribution baselines only; it never searched the vocabularies where 'delete an item and the next candidate is promoted' is standard practice (ranking and slate recommendation, corpus/coreset pruning with re-selection, remove-and-retrain evaluation). An AC will read that as searching the literature that supports the framing and not the literature that would deflate it.
